blogs.title: When a Young Adult With “Type 2” Diabetes Isn’t Type 2: Spotting HNF1A-MODY at the Bedside
blogs.description: This post would walk clinicians through the practical clues that should trigger suspicion for MODY in a young patient with hyperglycaemia: autosomal dominant family history, negative islet autoantibodies, preserved endogenous insulin secretion, glycosuria, and absence of clear insulin resistance. It would emphasize how MODY can masquerade as either type 1 or type 2 diabetes, especially in patients with borderline BMI or metabolic syndrome features, and propose a pragmatic bedside approach to deciding who merits genetic testing.

blogs.title: Autoantibodies Negative, C-Peptide Present—Now What? Interpreting the Grey Zone in Early-Onset Diabetes
blogs.description: This post would focus on the diagnostic tension created by supportive but imperfect biomarkers. Using this case, it would examine how to interpret glucagon-stimulated C-peptide, the limits of negative GAD and IA-2 antibodies, and why neither test alone rules in or rules out MODY or early type 1 diabetes. It would discuss how clinicians can combine phenotype, trajectory, and family history when laboratory data are suggestive but not definitive.

blogs.title: Precision Diabetes in Action: How a Genetic Diagnosis Changed Therapy
blogs.description: This post would analyze the management implications of confirming HNF1A-MODY. It would explore why the patient was initially treated as presumed type 2 diabetes, how genetic testing allowed insulin discontinuation, and the rationale for shifting toward incretin-based therapy. The discussion would place this case in the broader context of precision medicine in diabetes, where identifying the subtype can materially change drug choice, hypoglycaemia risk, counseling, and long-term follow-up.

blogs.title: Beyond Sulfonylureas: Are GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Underused in HNF1A-MODY?
blogs.description: This post would examine the evolving treatment paradigm for HNF1A-MODY. Although sulfonylureas are traditionally first-line, this case highlights successful use of a GLP-1 receptor agonist with excellent HbA1c reduction and avoidance of hypoglycaemia. The blog would review the physiologic rationale, the limited trial data comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists with sulfonylureas, and how declining beta-cell reserve, patient preferences, and safety considerations might influence therapy selection in real-world practice.

blogs.title: Glycosuria Without SGLT2 Inhibitors: The Renal Clue to HNF1A-MODY—and Why It Matters
blogs.description: This post would focus on glycosuria as more than a nonspecific diabetes finding. It would explain how HNF1A mutations lower the renal threshold for glucose via altered SGLT2 expression, making glycosuria an early diagnostic clue. It would then connect this physiology to prescribing implications, especially the potential hazards of SGLT2 inhibitors in HNF1A-MODY, including dehydration, genital infections, and ketoacidosis risk.

blogs.title: A Novel Variant, an Old Problem: What This Case Teaches About NGS and Variant Interpretation in MODY
blogs.description: This post would address the genomics side of the case: why next-generation sequencing is increasingly central to diagnosing atypical diabetes, and how clinicians should think about a previously unreported HNF1A variant. It would explain the role of ACMG criteria, segregation with disease, domain location, and computational tools in classifying novel variants, while highlighting the broader challenge that MODY remains underdiagnosed partly because testing is often reserved for patients who fit an imperfect clinical stereotype.
